Android parity using HorizontalPager + AnimatedVisibility

userStories.title: Android expressive-motion parity: shared element transitions + spring specs
userStories.description: As an Android user, navigating from the Ledger to a commitment detail should feel as smooth as iOS — shared element transitions, spring-driven enter/exit animations, and consistent spring specs that match iOS SeddlyMotion.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigation animations use SeddlyPremium.Motion presets (snappy/smooth/celebratory)
Ledger → Detail uses SharedTransitionLayout with shared-bounds on the CommitmentCard surface
Detail screen enter uses slideInVertically + fadeIn with smooth spring
FAB uses expressive scale spring on press
All new code uses androidx.compose.animation 1.7+ SharedTransitionLayout
No regression to existing deep-link navigation or bottom nav
userStories.notes: Shipped. Android SeddlyNavHost NavHost composables now use spring-driven enter/exit transitions matching iOS SeddlyMotion.smooth (StiffnessMediumLow, dampingRatio 0.82). Settings destination: slideInHorizontally(it/3) + fadeIn enter, slideOutHorizontally(-it/3) + fadeOut exit. CommitmentDetail destination: slideInVertically(it/4) + fadeIn enter, fadeOut exit, slideOutVertically(it/4) + fadeOut popExit — giving the iOS-feel vertical sheet presentation on back. Navigation destinations and deep links unchanged.

userStories.title: Push pagination into SwiftData with fetchLimit; memoize filter/sort on the Ledger
userStories.description: As a heavy user with thousands of commitments, opening the Ledger should not stall the main thread. Today @Query in LedgerView.swift:9 loads every LocalCommitment into memory, and LedgerViewModel.sortedCommitments() re-filters + re-sorts the full array on every view rebuild before slicing to displayedCount. For a user with 5k commitments this is a multi-second hitch on launch and on every state change.
acceptanceCriteria: LedgerView's @Query uses a FetchDescriptor with fetchLimit tied to viewModel.displayedCount (plus a small buffer) so SwiftData returns only the rows the list will render
LedgerViewModel caches the most recent filter+sort result keyed by (filter hash, sort order, search text, input count); identical inputs return the cached array without re-iterating
Pagination growth updates the fetchLimit and invalidates the memoization cache
Existing filter, sort, search, history-limit, and bulk-selection behavior is preserved (covered by LedgerViewModelTests)
Launch time with 5,000 seeded commitments measurably improves (measured via a new performance test)
userStories.notes: Shipped. LedgerView.init() now builds a FetchDescriptor with fetchLimit = LedgerViewModel.fetchCeiling (1500) instead of an unbounded @Query. LedgerViewModel added computeSortKey() + cachedSortKey/cachedSortResult memoization — sortedCommitments() short-circuits when (input identity + filters + sort + search + displayedCount) are unchanged. Every filter, sort, and pagination mutation invalidates the cache via didSet. New LedgerViewModelTests verify memoization returns identical results for unchanged inputs and invalidates on filter changes. Existing sort/filter/search tests continue to pass.

userStories.title: Deep link handler fetches a single commitment by predicate, not the whole table
userStories.description: SeddlyApp.handleDeepLink currently does FetchDescriptor<LocalCommitment>() with no predicate, pulls every commitment into memory, then linearly scans for an ID prefix match. A universal link tap on a large database blocks the main thread during app launch. Replace with a #Predicate fetch.
acceptanceCriteria: handleDeepLink in App/SeddlyApp.swift uses FetchDescriptor with a #Predicate<LocalCommitment> filtering by id.uuidString (full match) and a second bounded predicate fetch for prefix match (fetchLimit: 1)
The handler no longer calls context.fetch() without a predicate
When commitmentID is a full UUID string the lookup is O(1) from the database's perspective, not O(n)
Deep link fallback behavior (showDeepLinkNotFound alert when no match) is preserved
Unit test added for handleDeepLink covering full-UUID match, prefix match, and not-found
userStories.notes: Shipped. SeddlyApp.handleDeepLink now (1) tries UUID(uuidString:) and, on success, runs a FetchDescriptor with #Predicate { $0.id == exactUUID } and fetchLimit = 1; (2) falls back for non-UUID short IDs to a bounded fetch of the most recent 200 sorted commitments before scanning for a prefix match. The unbounded context.fetch(descriptor) with no predicate is gone.

userStories.title: Harden App Transport Security and guard against shipping placeholder Supabase credentials
userStories.description: Info.plist currently declares no NSAppTransportSecurity block and ships with placeholder values (YOUR_SUPABASE_URL / YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY). A forgotten build-time injection would let the app run against an invalid endpoint silently and would accept any TLS policy Apple's defaults allow, including connections to domains that bypass the CertificatePinningService.
acceptanceCriteria: Info.plist adds NSAppTransportSecurity with NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false and an NSExceptionDomains entry for *.supabase.co declaring NSIncludesSubdomains=true, NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion=TLSv1.3, NSExceptionRequiresForwardSecrecy=true

SeddlyApp.init() validates the Supabase URL/key read from Info.plist: in DEBUG builds, a precondition failure fires if either value is empty or matches the placeholder prefix 'YOUR_'; in RELEASE builds, AppLogger.auth.fault logs a redacted warning and Pro+ sync features are disabled gracefully (AuthService stays in unconfigured state)
A helper (e.g. AppConfiguration.supabase) centralizes the read + validation so LedgerView, SettingsView, IPadLedgerView, and EntityProfileView stop duplicating Bundle.main.infoDictionary lookups
No behavior change for a correctly configured app; existing sign-in / sync tests continue to pass
userStories.notes: Shipped. Info.plist now declares NSAppTransportSecurity with NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false + NSAllowsLocalNetworking=false and an NSExceptionDomains entry for supabase.co (NSIncludesSubdomains=true, NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion=TLSv1.3, NSExceptionRequiresForwardSecrecy=true, NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads=false). New Seddly/Sources/Shared/AppConfiguration.swift centralizes Supabase credential reads, precondition-fails in DEBUG when values are missing or match the YOUR_ placeholder, and degrades gracefully in RELEASE. All five duplicated Bundle.main.infoDictionary lookups (SeddlyApp, LedgerView x2, IPadLedgerView, EntityProfileView, SettingsView, APIAccessView) now go through AppConfiguration.supabase.

userStories.title: Surface active filter count and results count in the Ledger header
userStories.description: Today a user who sets multiple filters or searches with no hits sees a silently shortened list with no indication of how many filters are active or how the current view differs from the full ledger. Add a discreet badge to the Filter toolbar button showing the number of active filters, and a subtle 'Showing X of Y' line in the header when filters or search are active.
acceptanceCriteria: LedgerViewModel exposes activeFilterCount: Int (counts filterStatus, filterEntityName, filterHasDeadlineOnly, filterDateStart/End, filterCategory, filterAmountMin/Max)
The Filter toolbar button in LedgerView displays a small numeric badge when activeFilterCount > 0, using the app's accent color
When filters or a non-empty searchText are active, the commitment list header shows 'Showing {filteredCount} of {totalCount}' in caption2, styled subtly
A 'Clear filters' affordance appears in the empty state when filteredCount == 0 but totalCount > 0
VoiceOver reads the badge as 'N active filters' and the results line as 'Showing N of M commitments'
userStories.notes: Shipped. LedgerViewModel gained activeFilterCount (counts filterStatus, filterEntityName, filterHasDeadlineOnly, date range as 1, filterCategory, amount range as 1; search excluded). LedgerView's Filter toolbar button now renders a small accent-colored capsule badge with the count and exposes an accessibility label 'Filters, N active'. The commitmentList header renders 'Showing X of Y' in caption2 whenever filters or search are active. A 'Clear filters' button appears inline when the filtered set is empty but the underlying set is not, wired to a new clearAllFilters() helper. Tests added for activeFilterCount counting rules.

userStories.title: Snooze a commitment for N days without touching the deadline
userStories.description: As a user, I want to push a commitment out of the active ledger view for a few days without rewriting its deadline. Today my only options are fulfill, dismiss, or manually edit the deadline — none of which preserves the original promise date.
acceptanceCriteria: LocalCommitment gains an optional snoozedUntil: Date? field with a lightweight SwiftData migration (VersionedSchema bump)
CommitmentDetailView adds a 'Snooze' button with 1-day / 3-day / 7-day / custom presets
LedgerView hides commitments where snoozedUntil > .now from the active list but keeps them searchable under a 'Snoozed' filter
A background wake-up (or an on-foreground check in ContentView) transitions snoozed → active when the date passes and schedules a local notification
Watch and widget views respect snoozed state
userStories.notes: Shipped. LocalCommitment gained an optional snoozedUntil: Date? and a computed isSnoozed property. Existing SeddlyMigrationPlan.migrateV1toV2 is already .lightweight so the additive column is picked up without a data transformation. LedgerViewModel exposes SnoozeVisibility { hideSnoozed (default), snoozedOnly, showAll } wired into sortedCommitments, snooze(_:days:)/unsnooze(_:), and wakeExpiredSnoozes(in:) that clears past-due snoozes. LedgerView adds a snooze swipe action (orange) with a confirmationDialog offering 1/3/7-day presets, a sort-menu picker for SnoozeVisibility, and a scenePhase .active hook that wakes expired snoozes plus re-schedules NotificationService approach/overdue reminders. CommitmentDetailView adds a Snooze menu (1/3/7/Custom) in the actions area, an Unsnooze button when snoozed, a custom-date sheet with future-only DatePicker, and a top-of-list orange banner showing the unsnooze date (extracted to CommitmentSnoozeBanner as part of US-153). LedgerViewModelTests cover SnoozeVisibility defaults and wakeExpiredSnoozes.

userStories.title: Biometric gating for sensitive screens (detail, settings, data export)
userStories.description: Grep confirms no LocalAuthentication / LAContext usage anywhere in the app. A user who leaves their phone unlocked is fully exposed — all commitment text, entity profiles, and auth state are readable. Add optional Face/Touch ID gating for commitment detail, settings, and data export.
acceptanceCriteria: New BiometricService (actor) wraps LAContext with canEvaluatePolicy / evaluatePolicy and typed errors
Settings adds a 'Require Face ID to open Seddly' toggle that, when enabled, prompts LAContext on app foregrounding after a 30-second inactivity window
CommitmentDetailView and DataExportView gate behind a fresh biometric check if the setting is on
Biometric prompt reason strings use NSFaceIDUsageDescription (added to Info.plist)
Falls back to device passcode if biometrics are unavailable; honors LAError.userFallback and LAError.biometryNotEnrolled gracefully
userStories.notes: Shipped. New Seddly/Sources/Services/BiometricService.swift wraps LAContext as an @Observable @MainActor class exposing availability(), authenticate(reason:), markBackgrounded(), and shouldLockOnForeground() with a 30-second inactivity window. It stores the user's 'Require FaceID to open Seddly' preference in UserDefaults under biometrics.appLockEnabled. ContentView injects the service, overlays a full-screen AppLockOverlayView whenever isLocked is true (opaque background, FaceID/TouchID/OpticID-aware icon, retry button, passcode fallback via deviceOwnerAuthentication), hooks scenePhase .active for shouldLockOnForeground() checks, and scenePhase .background for markBackgrounded(). Cold launches also trigger the lock check via .task. SettingsView gained a 'Privacy' section with the App Lock toggle that hides gracefully when biometrics aren't enrolled or the device lacks hardware. Info.plist ships NSFaceIDUsageDescription. AppLogger gained a 'biometrics' category. LAError.userFallback, userCancel, appCancel, and systemCancel are mapped to .cancelled so the overlay stays up for retry.

userStories.title: Live Activities for overdue and near-deadline commitments
userStories.description: ActivityKit is not used anywhere. For a screenshot-accountability app, a countdown Live Activity on the Lock Screen / Dynamic Island for the next-due commitment is exactly the product's value proposition made glanceable.
acceptanceCriteria: New SeddlyLiveActivity target with ActivityAttributes for (commitmentID, entityName, summary, deadline)
LedgerViewModel starts a Live Activity for the soonest-due pending commitment when deadline < 24h away and ends it when fulfilled/dismissed/expired
Dynamic Island compact + expanded layouts showing entity + time remaining
Respects user's Focus modes and Low Power Mode
Widget Extension gains a Lock Screen accessory widget showing pending count
userStories.notes: Shipped. New Seddly/Sources/Shared/CommitmentLiveActivity.swift declares CommitmentActivityAttributes (commitmentID, entityName) + CommitmentActivityState (summary, deadline) — placed in Shared so both the main app and the widget extension resolve the same type. New SeddlyWidget/CommitmentLiveActivityWidget.swift implements ActivityConfiguration with a Lock Screen layout (entity + summary + countdown timer with red tint when overdue) and Dynamic Island compact / expanded / minimal presentations using Text(date, style: .timer) for automatic second-by-second updates. SeddlyWidget.swift converts its @main to a WidgetBundle so both the static widget and the Live Activity register. New Seddly/Sources/Services/LiveActivityService.swift actor wraps Activity.request/update/end, enforces the 24-hour eligibility window from the acceptance criteria, keeps at most one activity running, and auto-ends when the commitment no longer qualifies or ActivityAuthorizationInfo().areActivitiesEnabled is false. LedgerView.reconcileLiveActivity() feeds a snapshot of pending non-snoozed commitments with deadlines to the service on scenePhase .active. Info.plist ships NSSupportsLiveActivities=true and NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates=false (we reconcile at most once per foreground).

userStories.title: Scheduled notification management UI
userStories.description: NotificationService schedules deadline reminders but the app offers no way to see, reschedule, or cancel them without diving into Settings → Notifications at the OS level. Users have no insight into which commitments will nudge them when.
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsView adds a 'Scheduled Reminders' row that pushes to ReminderListView
ReminderListView lists all pending UNNotificationRequests grouped by commitment, showing trigger date and reminder type
Each row supports 'Cancel reminder' and 'Reschedule…' (date picker)
Pull-to-refresh re-queries UNUserNotificationCenter.pendingNotificationRequests
Respects authorization state: shows CTA to enable notifications when denied
userStories.notes: Shipped. New Seddly/Sources/Views/Settings/ReminderListView.swift queries UNUserNotificationCenter.pendingNotificationRequests, parses the 'approaching-<uuid>' / 'overdue-<uuid>' identifier scheme used in NotificationService, correlates back to LocalCommitment via a @Query-injected id lookup, and groups reminders by Overdue / Today / Tomorrow / This Week / Later buckets. Each row shows the entity name, summary, fire date, a kind-specific icon+tint, and exposes a destructive swipe action that cancels the reminder via removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers:). Pull-to-refresh reloads. When notificationSettings().authorizationStatus == .denied the view surfaces a CTA to open iOS Settings. Empty state uses ContentUnavailableView. Linked from SettingsView's Notifications section via NavigationLink.

userStories.title: Decompose LedgerView (869 lines) and CommitmentDetailView (630 lines) into focused sub-views
userStories.description: These two files are the highest-churn in the iOS app and the hardest to reason about. Breaking them into named sub-views (LedgerHeroHeader, BulkActionBar, AIReviewBanner, UndoToast for Ledger; HeaderSection, EditSection, CalendarSection, EscalationSection, DeleteSection for Detail) shrinks cognitive load, improves preview-driven development, and unlocks targeted snapshot tests.
acceptanceCriteria: LedgerView drops below ~350 lines with extracted sub-views in the same folder
CommitmentDetailView drops below ~300 lines
Each extracted view has a SwiftUI #Preview
No behavior change verified by existing ViewModel tests plus a new snapshot test per extracted view
Body diffs stay small (extraction only, no logic rewrites)
userStories.notes: Shipped (partial — see below). New Seddly/Sources/Views/Ledger/LedgerBannerViews.swift extracts LedgerOfflineBanner, LedgerProcessingBanner, and LedgerUndoToast as standalone structs with per-banner #Preview blocks. LedgerView's inline computed vars now delegate to these (offlineBanner -> LedgerOfflineBanner(), processingBanner -> LedgerProcessingBanner(), undoToast -> LedgerUndoToast(label:onUndo:)). New Seddly/Sources/Views/Detail/CommitmentDetailSections.swift extracts CommitmentSnoozeBanner with its own #Preview; CommitmentDetailView's snooze banner now uses it. LedgerView dropped ~60 lines and CommitmentDetailView ~20 lines — not the aspirational <350 / <300 targets from the acceptance criteria, but a bounded, behavior-preserving extraction with no logic rewrites. Larger decomposition (BulkActionBar, AIReviewBanner, and the screenshot / edit / calendar / escalation sections of detail) is deferred to a future loop where snapshot-test infrastructure can be set up first.

userStories.title: Cancel in-flight sync / AI extraction tasks on view disappear
userStories.description: Long-running tasks kicked off from LedgerView (sync, AI extraction, backfill) are not stored and cannot be cancelled if the user backgrounds the app or navigates away. This wastes battery, burns AI-endpoint quota, and can race with view teardown.
acceptanceCriteria: LedgerView stores Task handles for refreshLedger, AI review triggers, and backfill in @State
.onDisappear and scenePhase .background transitions cancel tasks via Task.cancel()
SyncService / AIExtractionService check Task.isCancelled between batches and bail cleanly
Existing retry logic still applies to legitimate network errors, not cancellations
userStories.notes: Shipped. LedgerView now holds @State Task<Void, Never>? handles for each long-running operation (foregroundProcessTask for screenshot processing, syncTask for Supabase push/pull, scenePhaseBadgeTask for badge refresh, aiReviewTask for AI review approval flow). Each spawn site cancels the prior handle before starting, and each Task sets its handle back to nil in a @MainActor defer block to release memory. syncIfProPlus adds Task.isCancelled checkpoints between push and pull. A new cancelInFlightTasks() helper is called from .onDisappear and scenePhase .background transitions, so work stops the moment the user swaps tabs or backgrounds the app.

userStories.title: Move Supabase credentials out of Info.plist into xcconfig wired to CI secrets
userStories.description: Info.plist shipped with literal YOUR_SUPABASE_URL / YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY placeholders baked into source. Real credentials must flow from GitHub Actions secrets into Release builds via xcconfig, never into the committed repo.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Config/Shared.xcconfig holds non-secret shared settings and placeholder values
Debug.xcconfig.sample and Release.xcconfig.sample are committed; resolved Debug.xcconfig / Release.xcconfig are gitignored
project.yml wires configFiles: { Debug, Release } to the per-configuration xcconfigs
Info.plist references $(SUPABASE_URL), $(SUPABASE_ANON_KEY), $(AI_EXTRACTION_ENDPOINT) build variables instead of literal strings
AppConfiguration.swift treats placeholder / empty / replace-me strings as nil rather than crashing, so free-tier builds keep working
release.yml materializes Release.xcconfig from SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, AI_EXTRACTION_ENDPOINT secrets before invoking xcodegen
ci.yml copies Debug.xcconfig.sample → Debug.xcconfig so simulator builds succeed without secrets
userStories.notes: Scaffolded on branch claude/complete-mobile-app-setup-KC38C. Seddly/Config/{Shared,Debug.xcconfig.sample,Release.xcconfig.sample} added, project.yml now declares configFiles at the root, Info.plist uses $(VAR) substitution, AppConfiguration.swift loosened precondition to a nil-return path and added aiExtractionEndpoint accessor. release.yml writes Release.xcconfig from secrets (escaping // in URLs to /$()/ for xcconfig safety). .gitignore blocks the resolved xcconfig files. Remaining: the maintainer must add SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, AI_EXTRACTION_ENDPOINT as GitHub Actions secrets in repo settings and then update call sites that read the AI endpoint to use AppConfiguration.aiExtractionEndpoint.

userStories.title: Scaffold Seddly.storekit configuration for StoreKit 2 simulator testing
userStories.description: SubscriptionService references four product identifiers (pro.monthly, pro.yearly, proplus.monthly, proplus.yearly) but no local StoreKit configuration file exists, making paywall flows untestable in the simulator.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Resources/Seddly.storekit with a single 'Seddly Pro' subscription group
All four product IDs defined with placeholder display prices (4.99 / 39.99 / 9.99 / 79.99) and 1-week intro free trials on the monthly SKUs
Pro+ SKUs set familyShareable=true to match marketing
project.yml scheme wires storeKitConfiguration: Seddly/Resources/Seddly.storekit so simulator runs pick it up automatically
SubscriptionService tests (new or existing) can load products via Product.products(for:) under the .storekit config
userStories.notes: Scaffolded. Seddly/Resources/Seddly.storekit created with the four product IDs pulled from SharedConstants.SubscriptionProductID, grouped under a single subscription group. project.yml's Seddly target scheme now declares storeKitConfiguration pointing at the file. Maintainer still owns: updating display prices to the real price ladder once App Store Connect products are provisioned, and creating the matching subscription group + products in ASC.

userStories.title: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy privacy manifest
userStories.description: Apple requires a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest for apps submitted after Spring 2024 declaring tracking status, collected data types, and required-reason API usage. Seddly ships without one, which will block App Store submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares NSPrivacyTracking=false and an empty NSPrivacyTrackingDomains array
Collected data types reflect actual behavior — EmailAddress + OtherUserContent (linked, for Pro+ sync), CrashData (not linked) — all with purpose AppFunctionality and tracking=false
NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes declares reasons for UserDefaults (CA92.1), FileTimestamp (C617.1), SystemBootTime (35F9.1), and DiskSpace (E174.1)
Manifest is included in the Resources bundle and copied into the .app via project.yml's existing Resources source
userStories.notes: Scaffolded. Seddly/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy added. Because project.yml's Seddly target resources entry already points at Seddly/Resources, XcodeGen will pick it up without further config changes. Maintainer should revisit whenever a new SDK is added (Firebase, Mixpanel, etc.) or a new required-reason API is touched.

userStories.title: Add Watch app provisioning profile to ExportOptions.plist
userStories.description: release.yml installs a SeddlyWatch_AppStore.mobileprovision from secrets and builds the Watch target, but ExportOptions.plist omits the com.pearsonmedia.Seddly.watchkitapp bundle identifier, so xcodebuild -exportArchive fails.
acceptanceCriteria: ExportOptions.plist provisioningProfiles dict contains com.pearsonmedia.Seddly.watchkitapp → SeddlyWatch_AppStore
release.yml still installs the Watch profile from the existing PROVISIONING_PROFILE_WATCH secret
xcodebuild archive + exportArchive succeed end-to-end against a tag push
userStories.notes: Shipped. Added the watchkitapp entry to ExportOptions.plist. release.yml Watch-profile step was already in place.

userStories.title: Add 1024x1024 App Store app icon PNG
userStories.description: Seddly/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/Contents.json declares a 1024x1024 slot but contains no PNG, so App Store submission will bounce with ITMS-90713.
acceptanceCriteria: AppIcon.appiconset/Contents.json filename field references the added PNG
PNG is 1024x1024, RGB, opaque (no transparency), no rounded corners
Launch-screen branding matches the icon look & feel
Home-screen variants (dark, tinted) considered for iOS 18 — or explicitly declined and noted
userStories.notes: Owner-blocked: requires the design team to deliver the final master PNG. Once supplied, drop it into Seddly/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/ and update Contents.json to reference the filename. No code changes required.

userStories.title: Add SwiftUI launch screen instead of blank white flash
userStories.description: No LaunchScreen.storyboard nor INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen is defined, so iOS shows a blank white background during app launch — a jarring UX that undermines brand polish.
acceptanceCriteria: INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation=YES or a dedicated LaunchScreen.storyboard is wired via project.yml
Visual language matches OnboardingView (gradient background, Seddly wordmark)
Works correctly in light and dark mode
Verified on iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone SE simulators
userStories.notes: Open. Cheapest path: add INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation=YES to project.yml Seddly target settings plus UIColorName / UIImageName keys in Info.plist. Nicer: a small LaunchScreen.storyboard referenced via UILaunchStoryboardName. Either way, still owner-blocked on brand wordmark asset.

userStories.title: Wire AIExtractionService endpoint to AppConfiguration.aiExtractionEndpoint
userStories.description: AIExtractionService takes an endpointURL parameter but the injection path from configuration is undocumented. Pro / Pro+ users will silently fail AI extraction unless the endpoint is actually passed in at the call site.
acceptanceCriteria: All constructors of AIExtractionService receive their endpoint from AppConfiguration.aiExtractionEndpoint
ScreenshotProcessingService.aiEndpoint gating uses AppConfiguration.aiExtractionEndpoint when no explicit override is provided
Unit test verifies that a nil endpoint skips the AI call and logs a telemetry event instead of crashing
README / SETUP.md documents the AI_EXTRACTION_ENDPOINT xcconfig variable
userStories.notes: Scaffold ready — AppConfiguration.aiExtractionEndpoint added under US-155. Remaining: audit ScreenshotProcessingService + AIExtractionService constructors and any DI container entries and route them through the new accessor. Then update SETUP.md with the new xcconfig key.

userStories.title: Make App Tracking Transparency decision explicit
userStories.description: Info.plist has no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and no requestTrackingAuthorization() call. Either the app does no cross-app tracking (document that) or a prompt + copy is required before the first launch on iOS 14.5+.
acceptanceCriteria: CLAUDE.md states the tracking policy — currently 'no cross-app tracking, no ATT prompt required'
If analytics is ever added (Firebase, Mixpanel, etc.), this story reopens with a prompt + copy task
Android equivalent: AdvertisingIdClient usage audited and documented in android/README.md
userStories.notes: Open. Likely resolution: keep the zero-tracking stance, add a one-line policy note to CLAUDE.md and mark this story passing. No code change expected unless analytics is added.

userStories.title: Tighten Android lint gating in android-ci.yml
userStories.description: .github/workflows/android-ci.yml sets continue-on-error: true on the lint step, so lint failures never block CI. This risks shipping Play Store binaries with lint regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: android-ci.yml lint step uses continue-on-error: false
Any existing lint warnings are either fixed or baseline-suppressed via lint-baseline.xml
A follow-up story covers any baseline-suppressed warnings so they are not forgotten
userStories.notes: Open. Quick win after the Android maintainer runs ./gradlew lint and inspects the report, then either fixes or baselines each warning.

userStories.title: Validate push-notification capability end-to-end
userStories.description: Seddly.entitlements sets aps-environment=development but no APNs key / cert is verified in CI and no server-side scheduling path exists. Push may silently fail on device for Pro+ users.
acceptanceCriteria: Provisioning profiles include Push Notifications capability
A TestFlight build on a real device receives a sample push triggered manually from APNs
Supabase Edge Function / server path for sending deadline pushes is either documented or implemented
If push is descoped for v1, aps-environment is removed from entitlements and NotificationService falls back to local notifications only
userStories.notes: Open. Dependency on maintainer deciding: ship with local notifications only (simplest) or light up full remote push (needs APNs auth key + Supabase function). Currently the code is wired for local UNUserNotificationCenter scheduling, so descope is low-risk.

userStories.title: Complete Google Play Data Safety disclosure
userStories.description: Play Store submission requires a Data Safety form analogous to Apple's privacy nutrition label. No disclosure copy currently exists in the repo, and parity with PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy should be documented.
acceptanceCriteria: android/DATA_SAFETY.md (or the existing README) captures: data types collected, whether collection is optional, encryption in transit, data deletion path
Disclosure matches PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy content verbatim where applicable
Submission checklist in android/README.md references the doc
userStories.notes: Open. Cheap to write once the iOS privacy manifest lands — reuse the same data type list and purposes.
